methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College launching workplace AI training signals distributed capability-building outside metro hubs, creating potential peer networks for deep AI fluency in traditionally underserved regions if program reaches beyond individual credentialing.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with AI Ready RVA demonstrates institutional commitment to broad-based AI education and community impact, potentially creating distributed peer learning networks that move beyond shallow platform adoption toward genuine capability development.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment in AI data center infrastructure in Henrico concentrates physical and capital resources in Richmond metro, deepening technical capability in established hubs while rural areas face energy constraints and limited access to the same infrastructure benefits.

signals.title: Virginia county asks all employees, including schools, to conserve power due to AI-driven electricity price hikes — state's 400-plus data centers steadily increasing demand, grid expansion, and pricing - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Northern Virginia counties imposing power conservation due to data center electricity demand reveals infrastructure strain even in wealthy tech hubs, signaling that concentration without adequate capacity planning creates constraints that prevent both depth and distribution from scaling.

signals.title: AI Has Already Arrived in Roanoke’s Classrooms. Here’s What Parents, Students, and Workers Should Know. - The Roanoke Rambler
signals.signal_reading: AI already arriving in Roanoke classrooms through platform tools suggests broad but potentially shallow adoption, where students and educators consume AI services without necessarily building deep technical capability or understanding underlying systems.
